points.name: Hill Cumorah (New York)
points.note: The New York hill associated with Joseph Smith’s account of obtaining the plates. Its equivalence to the battlefield in Mormon 6 is a separate, disputed identification.

points.name: Zarahemla
points.note: North of the Nephi border; Gideon is across Sidon. City/land extent and exact river separation are unknown.

points.name: Land of Nephi
points.note: South of Zarahemla across the wilderness. The position of its city within the larger land is unknown.

points.name: Land of Bountiful
points.note: North of Zarahemla and south of Desolation. The city is not necessarily the center of the land.

points.name: Desolation
points.note: North of Bountiful; extent and distances not specified.

points.name: Sidon
points.note: Book of Mormon river, not the Phoenician city. Head near Manti/southern border; a northward reach is inferred. Mouth and complete course are unknown.

points.name: Manti
points.note: Near the head of Sidon, by the southern wilderness. Exact position unknown.

points.name: Melek
points.note: West of Sidon; Ammonihah lies three days north of the land of Melek. These are not surveyed city-to-city endpoints.

points.name: Ammonihah
points.note: Three days north from Melek; distance depends on travel rate and the departure point.

points.name: Gideon (land)
points.note: Across Sidon from Zarahemla, east of the river in the valley. Diagram spacing is illustrative.

points.name: Jershon
points.note: East by the sea, south of Bountiful; broad land, not a precisely located city.

points.name: Antionum
points.note: East of Zarahemla, nearly bordering the sea, south of Jershon; wilderness to its south.

points.name: Mulek (city)
points.note: On the eastern front; near enough to Bountiful for the described maneuvers. Exact mileage unknown.

points.name: Moroni (city)
points.note: By the east sea near the southern boundary; distinguish the city from Moroni the person.

points.name: Nephihah
points.note: Between Moroni and Aaron; this diagram places Aaron inland as an illustrative choice.

points.name: Aaron (eastern city)
points.note: Borders Nephihah; not automatically the Aaron in Alma 8:13.

points.name: Lehi (city)
points.note: Northward along the eastern seashore; borders Morianton.

points.name: Morianton (city)
points.note: Neighbor of Lehi on the seashore. North/south ordering between these neighbors is not fixed here by the text.

points.name: Waters of Mormon
points.note: Associated with Alma’s refuge. Exact distance and direction from Nephi are not supplied; western offset is only for readability.

points.name: Helam
points.note: Reached after eight days in Alma’s escape. Position along a generally northward diagram route is illustrative, not a stated bearing.

points.name: Valley of Alma
points.note: An all-day journey from Helam; then twelve wilderness days before Zarahemla. Bearing is not supplied.

points.name: First inheritance
points.note: West in Nephi by the seashore. This does not determine a transoceanic landing route.

points.note: A settlement near the waters of Mormon; destroyed by waters. Distinct from Jerusalem in the Old World.

points.name: Nephi (city)
points.note: City of Nephi / Lehi-Nephi; distinct from the larger land of Nephi. Kaminaljuyu is a published candidate, not an established identification.

routes.note: Escape from the Mormon-area refuge; not a measured Nephi-city segment.
The text says they traveled all day.
Wilderness travel; not a straight line.
From the land of Melek; northward, endpoint precision unknown.

candidates.name: Southern Mexico / Tehuantepec
candidates.fit: An isthmus, two ocean coasts and southern highlands make this a useful comparison region.
candidates.problem: The selected coast anchors are roughly 230 km apart. That is much longer than 1½ days at the illustrative 10–50 km/day rates. A shorter partial line, unusually fast travel, or other reading is required. Compass alignment and the identity of Sidon remain unresolved.

candidates.name: Panama / northern South America
candidates.fit: A short ocean-to-ocean land connection is a closer match to a short crossing under the illustrative daily-distance assumptions.
candidates.problem: Width alone does not locate Zarahemla, Nephi or Sidon. The local land axis is not simply north–south. Modern canals and reservoirs cannot be used as ancient evidence.

candidates.name: Great Lakes / Niagara
candidates.fit: The selected lake-to-lake separation is short; this region is relevant to Great Lakes proposals and New York Cumorah traditions.
candidates.problem: It requires inland lakes to serve as seas. A short connection alone does not satisfy all land, river, coast and directional constraints. Great Lakes and Mississippi/Ohio Heartland proposals are distinct models.

candidates.name: Mississippi / Ohio Heartland
candidates.fit: Relevant to nineteenth-century interpretive traditions and proposals involving the Mississippi and Ohio valleys.
candidates.problem: No single agreed narrow-neck transect is assumed here. Hopewell archaeology documents Indigenous societies; it does not itself identify Nephite cities. Modern U.S. borders are not a textual geographical constraint.
